emails.subject: quick question

What do you actually want help with right now?

Hit reply and tell me in a sentence or two.

I read every reply myself. I'll write back with a straight answer. If it's easier to show than tell, I'll record you a short video instead.

emails.subject: The part that scares beginners
emails.body:
The scary part of owning a website is DNS. That's the setting that connects your domain to your site. Get it wrong and your site, or your email, can stop working.

So the Launchpad has a rule: Claude copies every existing record first, then stops and asks you before it changes anything. It also comes with a one-page Rollback Card that shows how to undo the switch in about two minutes.

You keep control the whole way.

Rob

first_sale_series.name: First-Sale Cheat Sheet: delivery + 3 follow-ups
first_sale_series.trigger: Added to audience: First-Sale Cheat Sheet Leads

emails.subject: Your First-Sale Cheat Sheet
emails.body:
Here it is: {SITE}/r/first-sale/

There's a PDF on the same page if you'd rather print it and tape it to your monitor.

Your only job today is step 1. Pick one problem. Not your passion. A small, annoying problem somebody would pay $7 to make go away this week.

Stuck? Paste this into ChatGPT or Claude:

"List 20 small problems [your audience] complains about online. Which 3 would someone pay $7 to fix this week?"

One favor. Hit reply and tell me the problem you picked. One line is fine. It tells your inbox I'm a real person, so the next emails land where you'll see them. And I'll tell you straight if it's a good first product.

Rob

emails.subject: the smallest thing
emails.body:
Most first products die because they're too big.

Somebody picks a good problem. Then they spend six weeks building a course nobody asked for. Then they quit.

Step 2 on your cheat sheet is the fix. One page. One afternoon.

Here's the test: can you finish it before dinner? If not, cut it in half. Then cut it again.

Not this: "The Complete Instagram Growth System."
This: "5 Story frames that get DMs for home bakers." One page.

Paste this into any AI to get a first draft:

"Write a one-page fix for [problem]. Plain words. Steps only. Include one example."

Then rewrite it in your own words. Price it at $7. Done.

Reply and tell me what you're building. I'll tell you what to cut.

Rob

emails.subject: the message that gets the first sale
emails.body:
Steps 5 and 6 are where first sales actually happen. Conversations.

Most people skip them. They post their product once, hear crickets, and decide it doesn't work.

Here's the difference.

The message that gets ignored:
"Hey! I made a product you'll love. Want to buy it?"

The message that gets answered:
"Saw your comment about [problem]. Is that still bugging you?"

When they say yes:
"I made a one-page fix for exactly that. It's $7. Want the link?"

That's it. No pitch until they've told you the problem is real.

Where do you find them? Facebook groups, comment sections, anywhere your person is already complaining. Answer five real questions there first, for free. Then start your ten conversations.

Ten messages won't guarantee a sale. But almost nobody sends ten, and that's why almost nobody gets one.

Rob

emails.subject: still stuck on step 1?
emails.body:
If you've read the cheat sheet and you're still stuck on step 1, you're not alone. Picking the problem is the hardest part.

So here's a shortcut: a problem that's already proven.

YouTubers and video creators hate making on-screen graphics. Lower thirds, title cards, captions. Most of them would happily pay somebody else to do it.

With AI software, you can make those graphics without being an editor and sell it as a one-person service.

I wrote a short guide on exactly how: who buys, what to message them, and what to charge. It's called The Overlay Agency, and it's $4.

{SITE}/overlay-agency/

Full disclosure: I co-own Grafsy, the software the guide recommends, so I earn if you buy it. That's why the guide only costs $4. Weigh it with that in mind.

And if you already picked your problem, ignore this and go send your ten messages.

Rob

emails.subject: The Robot Tells (your checklist)
emails.body:
Here it is: {SITE}/r/robot-tells/

12 giveaways that tell people a robot wrote your post, with a fix for each one.

Don't read all 12 today. Do this instead:

Take the last thing you posted. Check it against tells 1, 4 and 5. The throat-clearing opener, the fancy words, the dashes. Those three show up in almost every AI draft.

Fix just those and post the new version. That's it.

One favor. Hit reply and tell me which tell you caught in your own writing. One line is fine. It tells your inbox I'm a real person, so the next emails don't land in spam.

Rob

emails.subject: delete your first sentence
emails.body:
Quickest fix on the whole checklist:

Delete the first sentence of your post.

AI almost always opens by clearing its throat. "In today's world..." "Let's talk about..." "Have you ever wondered..."

The real post usually starts at sentence two.

Not this: "In today's fast-paced world, building an audience matters more than ever."
This: "Nobody followed me for the first 90 days."

Try it on your next draft before you post. If sentence two can stand on its own, you just made the post better in four seconds.

Rob

emails.subject: posts that sound human, and then what?
emails.body:
Fixing the robot tells gets people to stop scrolling. It doesn't make you money by itself.

For that you need something to sell, even something tiny.

If you don't have that yet, I made a free one-page cheat sheet for it. Seven steps from "I have nothing to sell" to your first buyer, with an AI prompt for each step.

{SITE}/first-sale/

No cost. Same as this checklist.

And if you already have an offer, ignore this and go post something that sounds like you.

Rob

emails.subject: Your AI Word List
emails.body:
Here it is: {SITE}/r/ai-word-list/

The words that get people to reply, call or buy, grouped by the job they do, with a weak and a stronger example for each.

Start with group 1, the words that get a reply. Use one in the first line of your next DM or comment.

Not this: "Hi, I help people grow their business. Interested?"
This: "Quick question. Saw your post about your first launch. What's been the hardest part so far?"

One rule with all of it: only use a word if it's true. Fake urgency costs you more than it earns.

One favor. Hit reply and tell me which word you're trying first. One line is fine. It tells your inbox I'm a real person, so the next emails don't land in spam.

Rob

emails.subject: the most underrated word
emails.body:
If you only use one word from the list, use "because."

A claim on its own sounds like a pitch. A claim with a reason sounds like a fact.

Not this: "This method really works."
This: "This works because you message people who already said they have the problem."

Put "because" right after your biggest claim in your next post. Then give one real reason. A number, a test you ran, something you saw.

That's group 6 on your list if you want more like it.

Rob

emails.subject: good words, nothing to sell?
emails.body:
The word list makes people reply. But a reply only turns into money if you have something to offer them.

If you don't have that yet, I made a free one-page cheat sheet for it. Seven steps from "I have nothing to sell" to your first buyer, with an AI prompt for each step.

{SITE}/first-sale/

No cost. Same as the word list.

And if you already have an offer, ignore this and go use "quick question" on ten people today.

Rob
